Public proof supplements

These supplements complete the notation and written derivations missing from the earlier selected-result delivery. They state ordinary mathematical proofs and preserve every conditional supplier. The paper arguments are not thereby new Lean formalizations. Use each result page together with its linked supplements.

Foundation and residual services

  • Canonical definitions: recurrence, time boundaries, labels, ghosts, tokens and owner inventories.
  • Ghost tokens and owner transport: complete ledgers, incidence matching, dated stock, source graph/forest and immortal limitations.
  • Source time and tightness: E/F context, penultimate capacity, actual death injection, predecessor and fresh-permutation scopes.

Abstract models and full private history

  • Count-clock implication and abstract boundary: scaling-limit proof and explicit 170-residue counterexample.
  • Finite MEX and window models: zero-MEX owners, periodic rescued queues, graph/window conventions and conditional consumers.
  • Private history and relay resources: source packing, corrected exit map, four sources and exact conditional relay/domain accounting.

Counting and finite certificates

  • Counting service budget: complete baseline physical-service budget and optimizer.
  • Counting extremizer theorem: defined deficits, disjoint source-target gain and exact liminf degree-eight result.
  • Finite certificate induction: actual legal reply families, periodic proof, lag211 induction and scoped shell criterion.
  • Lag124 proof: complete finite-reduction, context traces and forced-Q argument.
  • Portable finite certificate data: exact inputs and separate replay scope.

Pell and block/count coordinates

  • Pell recurrences: exact windows, capped contraction, finite rigidity and positive masked response hypotheses.
  • Block ghosts and C50: all block/young/pool definitions and the exact orbit/lineage/absence flux identities.

The canonical foundation, existing-slope derivation, and strict-liminf derivation retain their own mathematical scopes. An accepted conditional implication does not supply its canonical hypotheses. Open Q=o(n), direct-Q A1 and the original m<=5 assertion remain outside the selected theorem set.
